name: Loop header explicitly bounded by username.length() counts regardless of index arithmetic errors vs index must advance and stay in range
side_a: Do not deduct when the loop header itself is written against the username's length (e.g. `while (i < username.length())` / `while (i <= username.length())`) and the body reads username by index — off-by-one bounds (`<=`), out-of-range reads (`charAt(i + 1)`), or a branch that forgets to increment `i` are correctness/runtime bugs, not failures to 'consider multiple parts or indices in the context of a loop'.
side_b: Deduct when the index in a length-bounded loop can fail to advance or reads past the end, on the grounds that the loop does not actually traverse multiple valid indices of username.

name: Loop that would not compile (illegal iteration target / uninitialized accumulator) still counts vs compilable code required
side_a: Do not deduct for a loop whose header or body is type-invalid — e.g. `for (char character : username)` iterating a String/StringBuilder directly, with `username.delete(character)` and an uninitialized `String finalName` — as long as the written construct plainly intends to visit each character of username.
side_b: Deduct when the loop cannot compile as written (username is not an array/Iterable, accumulator never initialized), since no loop over username's characters actually executes.

name: Indexed charAt scan that pins the hyphen's position vs for-each over a char value with no index (and no real String call)
side_a: If the response walks the username with an explicit integer index and a String accessor (e.g., `username.charAt(i)` / `username.charAt(i + 1)` compared to '-'), the hyphen's location is identified by that index variable — award B2 (no_deduct), even if the loop bounds or increments are buggy (off-by-one, `i <= username.length()`, `i += 1` instead of `i += 2`), since those errors are judged under B3.
side_b: If the response iterates with an enhanced for over the String itself (`for (char character : username)`), only comparing the loop's char value to '-', no index ever exists, the construct is not legal on a String, and no String method is called to locate the hyphen — deduct B2.

name: Loop that throws / never terminates (no value ever returned) vs. loop that safely terminates and returns something
side_a: No_deduct when the accumulation loop always stays in bounds and is guaranteed to advance to termination, so the method actually reaches its `return` and hands back a shortened string (judge only whether that string is right).
side_b: Deduct when the written loop cannot deliver a value at all: a look-ahead index such as `charAt(i + 1)` is evaluated while `i` can reach `length()-1` (or the bound is `i <= username.length()`), throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, or a branch of the loop body fails to advance the counter so the loop spins forever. A runtime-fatal loop forfeits B3 regardless of how plausible the concatenation logic looks.

name: Builds the result with valid String operations vs. treats `username` as an array/mutable buffer
side_a: No_deduct when the shortened name is produced by legitimate String operations (charAt/substring/concatenation), even if a method is named or parameterized sloppily, because the mechanism for producing the returned string is still a real String construction.
side_b: Deduct when the response treats the String as something it is not — iterating it with an enhanced for-loop as if it were a char array, or calling a mutator like `delete(...)` to remove characters in place — and/or returns an accumulator that was declared without being initialized to "", so the constructed value is not a well-formed String build.
